claim: The Legislative Assembly holds an organizational session in December after the election, then recesses until the first Tuesday after the third day in January or another date set by law, no later than 11 January
quote: shall thereafter recess until twelve noon on the first Tuesday after the third day in January or at such other time as may be prescribed by law but not later than the eleventh day of January

claim: No regular session may exceed eighty natural days during the biennium
quote: No regular session of the legislative assembly may exceed eighty natural days during the biennium.

claim: By statute the assembly reconvenes at noon on the first Tuesday after the third day in January of the year after the organizational session, or on a date the legislative management picks between 2 and 11 January
quote: The legislative assembly shall reconvene at twelve noon on the first Tuesday after the third day in January of the year following the organizational session

claim: The legislative management may instead pick a reconvening date no earlier than 2 January and no later than 11 January
quote: not earlier than January second nor later than January eleventh of the year following the organizational session

claim: Most laws take effect on 1 August after filing with the secretary of state unless the act says otherwise or is an emergency measure
quote: takes effect on August first after its filing with the secretary of state

claim: During the session a bill becomes law if the governor neither signs nor vetoes it within three legislative days
quote: a bill becomes law if the governor neither signs nor vetoes it within three legislative days after its delivery to the governor

claim: After the session the governor has fifteen days, Saturdays and Sundays excepted, to act on a bill
quote: vetoes it within fifteen days, Saturdays and Sundays excepted, after its delivery to the governor

claim: The general election is the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of even-numbered years
quote: on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of each even-numbered year

claim: The primary is the second Tuesday in June of every general election year and nominates county officers and county commissioners among others
quote: On the second Tuesday in June of every general election year, a primary election must be held

claim: The June primary nominates county officers and county commissioners
quote: judges of the supreme court and district court, county officers, and county commissioners

claim: All elective county officers are elected at the general election before their terms expire
quote: All elective state, district, and county officers, and the United States senators, and the members of the United States house of representatives, must be elected at the general election

claim: No reference to party may be made in the petition of a candidate for an elective county office or for supreme or district court judge
quote: No reference may be made to a party ballot or to the party affiliation of a candidate in a petition and affidavit filed by or on behalf of a candidate for nomination in the primary election to an elective county office

claim: Candidates for those offices appear on a separate no-party primary ballot without party designation
quote: must be placed on the ballot without party designation

claim: The no-party primary advances the top vote-getters up to twice the number of seats, and partisan nominations may not be made for those offices
quote: who total twice the number of available positions for the office if that many individuals are candidates for nomination

claim: Partisan nominations may not be made for county, judicial and the other no-party offices
quote: Partisan nominations may not be made for any of the offices mentioned in section 16.1-11-08.

claim: The general election carries a separate no-party ballot for candidates nominated on the no-party primary ballot
quote: There must be a separate no-party ballot at the general election upon which must be placed the names of all candidates who have been nominated on the no-party primary ballot

claim: The primary uses one consolidated ballot with a section for each party; voting in more than one party's section rejects the party ballot but no-party and measure votes still count
quote: If you vote in more than one political party's section, your Political Party Ballot will be rejected; however, all votes on the No Party and Measure Ballots will still be counted.

claim: The primary ballot is one consolidated ballot with sections for all parties
quote: At the primary election there may be only one ballot containing the separate sections for all parties or principles.

claim: To be nominated in the primary a candidate needs at least as many votes as the petition signatures required for that office
quote: receives a number of votes at least equal to the number of signatures required on a petition

claim: Unless the law says otherwise, the candidate with the most votes is elected
quote: the individual receiving the highest number of votes for any office is deemed elected to that office

claim: Approval voting and ranked-choice voting may not be used to elect or nominate anyone to local, state or federal office
quote: Approval voting or ranked-choice voting may not be used in an election held within this state to elect or nominate a candidate to any local, state, or federal elective office.

claim: A local ordinance that conflicts with the ban is void, including one adopted under a home rule charter
quote: including an ordinance enacted or adopted under a home rule charter, which conflicts with this section is void

claim: There is no voter registration: the voter-list procedure may not be used to require registration
quote: The procedure provided for in this section may not be used to require the registration of electors.

claim: A voter must be a resident who has lived in the precinct at least thirty days before the election
quote: A resident of this state who has resided in the precinct at least thirty days immediately preceding any election.

claim: A voter must meet the identification requirements of section 16.1-01-04.1
quote: An elector seeking to vote in an election must meet the identification requirements specified in section 16.1-01-04.1.

claim: The secretary of state keeps a central voter file linked with county auditors
quote: A permanent, centralized electronic database of voters, to be known as the central voter file

claim: Independent candidates get on the general election ballot by certificate of nomination by petition, for any office except one on the no-party ballot, and appear as independent nominations
quote: except for an office appearing on the no-party ballot, may be made as provided by this section

claim: Names nominated by petition appear on the ballot as independent nominations, except presidential candidates
quote: names of nominees so nominated must appear on the ballot as independent nominations

claim: Only qualified electors of the state, district, county or subdivision may sign a nominating petition
quote: Only qualified electors of the state, district, county, or other political subdivision, as the case may be, may sign nominating petitions.

claim: A voter may sign independent nominating petitions for more than one candidate for the same office
quote: except an individual may sign a certificate of nomination by petition for more than one individual for each office

claim: A candidate defeated in the primary may not appear on the general election ballot for the same office
quote: who was defeated for the nomination may not have that individual's name printed upon the official ballot at the ensuing general election for the same office

claim: City elections are held on the second Tuesday in June of each even-numbered year
quote: Biennial municipal elections must be held on the second Tuesday in June in each even-numbered year.

claim: A city must agree with its county or counties on a single canvassing board, shared election staff and costs
quote: The governing body of a city shall enter into an agreement with the governing body of the county or counties in which the city lies

claim: No party reference may appear in the nominating petition of a candidate for city office
quote: No reference may be made to a party ballot nor to the party affiliation of a candidate in a petition to be filed by or in behalf of a candidate for nomination to a public office in any incorporated city in this state.

claim: City candidates are nominated by petition filed with the city auditor; signers must live in the ward if elected by ward, or the city if at large
quote: Qualified electors who sign a petition must reside within the ward or precinct in and for which that officer is to be elected, if the election is by wards, or within the corporate limits of the city, if the officer is elected at large.

claim: A city candidate may run for only one city office at an election
quote: A candidate may run for only one office in a city at any given election.

claim: The city auditor places only the names of the persons nominated on the ballot
quote: The auditor of the city shall place only the names of the persons nominated upon the ballot.

claim: City elections otherwise follow the rules for electing county officers
quote: by the laws of this state applicable to elections and contests in the case of county officers

claim: Municipalities are cities: the term includes all cities and no other political subdivision
quote: "Municipal corporation" or "municipality" includes all cities organized under the laws of this state, but shall not include any other political subdivision.

claim: Council cities are governed by a city council of the mayor and council members
quote: The governing body of a city operating under the council form of government is the city council, which is composed of the mayor and council members.

claim: A council city has at least three council members, a number that can change by vote
quote: The number of council members is not less than three.

claim: In council cities of 600 or fewer the council is elected at large; otherwise by ward unless a city of 5,000 or fewer opts for at large
quote: In cities containing six hundred inhabitants or less, the council members must be elected at large.

claim: A council city of up to 5,000 people may elect all council members at large by ordinance
quote: the governing body of a city having a population not exceeding five thousand and which is operating under the council form of government may provide by ordinance for the election of all council members at large

claim: Council members serve four-year terms, staggered so about half are elected at each election
quote: Council members shall hold office for four years and until their successors are elected and qualified.

claim: Council terms are arranged so about half the council is elected at each election
quote: one-half of the council members in any city, as nearly as practicable, are elected in any one election

claim: The mayor of a council city serves four years
quote: The mayor shall be a qualified elector within the city and shall hold office for four years

claim: A council city must elect a mayor and its council members, and may choose to have an elected municipal judge
quote: Each city operating under the council form of government may choose to have a municipal judge who is elected.

claim: In council cities the city auditor is appointed by the mayor with council approval, not elected
quote: The mayor, with the approval of the city council, shall appoint the following officers:

claim: Commission cities are governed by a board of city commissioners: a president and at least three commissioners
quote: is the board of city commissioners which is composed of the president of the board of city commissioners and not less than three city commissioners

claim: Commission members are elected at large, not by ward
quote: The members of the board of city commissioners must be elected at large and not by wards.

claim: Commissioners and the president serve four-year terms starting 1 July, about half elected every two years
quote: Each commissioner and the president of the board of city commissioners shall hold office for four years commencing on the first day of July of the year in which the officer was elected

claim: Under the modern council form the council has at least four members, one the mayor, elected at large or by wards to four-year terms
quote: which is composed of not less than four members, one of whom is the mayor, all elected at large or by wards

claim: Modern council terms are four years starting 1 July
quote: The terms of members of the council is four years, commencing on the first of July of the year in which the member was elected

claim: A city may adopt a city manager plan
quote: CITY MANAGER PLAN

claim: The size of a city governing body can be changed by a vote of the city's electors, started by the governing body or a petition
quote: shall submit the question of increasing or decreasing the number of members of the city governing body to the electors of the city

claim: A city that sets up a municipal court must provide by ordinance for electing at least one judge
quote: The governing body shall, by ordinance, provide for the election of at least one full-time or part-time judge.

claim: A municipal judge is elected to a four-year term
quote: A municipal judge must be elected to serve a term of four years

claim: Any city may adopt a home rule charter; there is no population threshold
quote: Any city may frame, adopt, amend, or repeal home rule charters as provided in this chapter.

claim: A city home rule charter supersedes state law except in matters pertaining to city elections
quote: except for matters pertaining to city elections, supersede within the territorial limits and other jurisdiction of the city any law of the state in conflict with the charter

claim: A home rule city ordinance on city elections that conflicts with state law is void, with one exception in section 40-05.1-06(9)
quote: any ordinance enacted or adopted by a city pertaining to city elections under a home rule charter in conflict with state law is void

claim: The one election exception: a home rule city may set the signature thresholds for city candidates' nominating petitions
quote: Notwithstanding section 40-21-07, to provide for all matters pertaining to signature thresholds for nominating petitions for candidates for city offices

claim: A home rule charter may set the city's form and structure of government, including its governing body and executive officer
quote: To provide for change, selection, or creation of its form and structure of government, including its governing body, executive officer, and city officers.

claim: Home rule for counties and cities exists only as the legislature provides and only after voter approval
quote: The legislative assembly shall provide by law for the establishment and exercise of home rule in counties and cities.

claim: A city park district is governed by an elected board of five or three park commissioners with four-year terms starting 1 July
quote: by a board of park commissioners consisting of five or three members

claim: Park commissioners serve four-year terms
quote: each commissioner shall hold office for a term of four years and until a successor is elected and qualified

claim: Park commissioners are elected at the regular city elections
quote: After the first board is elected, the members of the board must be elected at the regular city elections.

claim: A park district is known as the park district of the city
quote: A park district shall be known as "park district of the city of ___________".

claim: North Dakota's counties are those whose names and boundaries are fixed in sections 11-01-02 through 11-01-54 (53 counties)
quote: Sections 11-01-02 through 11-01-54 shall be deemed to show the names and boundaries of the several counties of this state

claim: Each organized county has a board of county commissioners of three to five members
quote: Each organized county shall have a board of county commissioners which shall consist of not less than three nor more than five members.

claim: Each commissioner is chosen by the voters of the district where the commissioner lives, unless the county elects at large
quote: Each county commissioner shall be chosen by the qualified electors of the district of which the commissioner is a resident

claim: Voters may switch the county to at-large commissioner elections by a sixty percent vote
quote: If approved by sixty percent of the qualified electors voting at such election, all county commissioner districts in the county must be immediately dissolved

claim: County commissioners serve four-year terms
quote: A county commissioner shall hold office for the term of four years

claim: Any elective county office has a four-year term, and the sheriff must be elected
quote: Any elective office provided for by the counties shall be for a term of four years.

claim: The office of sheriff must be elected
quote: The office of sheriff shall be elected.

claim: Until a county adopts an optional form, a board of county commissioners governs it
quote: Until one of the optional forms of county government is adopted by any county, the fiscal and administrative affairs of the county shall be governed by a board of county commissioners

claim: By default a county has an auditor, recorder, treasurer and the board of commissioners, plus an elected state's attorney and sheriff, unless it has combined or redesignated offices
quote: each county must have an elected state's attorney and an elected sheriff

claim: Recorder, auditor, treasurer, sheriff and state's attorney are elected on a four-year cycle
quote: except the recorder, county auditor, treasurer, sheriff, and state's attorney, who must be chosen in 1966 and every four years thereafter

claim: In counties of 6,000 or fewer people, the recorder is also ex officio clerk of the district court
quote: In counties having a population of six thousand or less, the recorder also serves as ex officio clerk of the district court.

claim: Voters may make the state's attorney appointive
quote: the county auditor shall place the question of appointing the state's attorney on the ballot

claim: A county may combine, separate or make appointive its elective offices without home rule; the sheriff is excluded
quote: Redesignate an elective county office as an appointive office or an appointive office as an elective office.

claim: The sheriff is excluded from the office combination chapter
quote: The office of sheriff is excluded from the application of this chapter.

claim: Counties may share a combined elective office with other counties
quote: A county may combine any county elective office with one or more elective offices of one or more other counties

claim: The county coroner is appointed by the board of county commissioners
quote: The board of county commissioners shall appoint a coroner for a term of five years.

claim: Counties may adopt a county manager form, with the manager appointed or elected
quote: Any county in this state is authorized to adopt one of the following county manager forms of government:

claim: Counties may adopt the consolidated office form of county government
quote: Any county in this state may adopt the county consolidated office form of government

claim: A county home rule charter supersedes conflicting state law except in matters pertaining to county elections
quote: except for matters pertaining to county elections, must be liberally construed to supersede

claim: A home rule county ordinance on county elections that conflicts with state law is void
quote: Any ordinance enacted or adopted by a county pertaining to county elections under a home rule charter in conflict with state law is void.

claim: A county charter may not change the structure of township government without the township board's consent
quote: or to change the structure of township government in any organized civil township, without the consent of the board of supervisors of the township

claim: Under a county charter, an elected office may be eliminated or combined only with voter approval or the combination procedures; sheriff and state's attorney cannot be made appointive this way
quote: This subsection does not authorize a county to redesignate the elected offices of sheriff and state's attorney as appointed

claim: Township law does not apply inside incorporated cities
quote: Nothing contained in this title applies in any way to any portion of the state which is embraced within the limits of any incorporated city.

claim: A civil township is organized only after a petition and a vote of the electors of the congressional township
quote: If a majority of the votes cast approve of organization, the township must then be organized

claim: Township voters can dissolve the township at the annual meeting
quote: If a majority of votes cast at the township meeting are in favor of dissolution, the township ceases to be a corporation on the next succeeding January first.

claim: Township electors hold an annual township meeting in March
quote: The electors of each township annually shall assemble and hold a township meeting in the month of March

claim: Supervisors, treasurer and clerk are elected by ballot at the meeting
quote: The supervisors, treasurer, and clerk in each township must be elected by ballot.

claim: The township ballot carries the names of the persons voted for and their offices, with no party
quote: the names of the persons voted for and the offices to which such persons are intended to be chosen

claim: At a township election the person with the most votes is declared elected
quote: The person having the greatest number of votes for an office must be declared elected.

claim: Only people qualified to vote at general elections may vote at township meetings
quote: A person may not vote at any township meeting unless that person is qualified to vote at general elections therein.

claim: Township electors may expand the board of supervisors from three to five
quote: the electors of the township may approve expansion of the board of township supervisors from three to five members

claim: Township officers are three or five supervisors, a clerk, an assessor and a treasurer
quote: The elected officers of a civil township must be:

claim: On a three-member board one supervisor is elected each year for a three-year term
quote: In townships with three-member boards of township supervisors, one supervisor must be elected at each annual township meeting and shall hold office for a term of three years.

claim: Other township officers serve two-year terms
quote: The other elective officers must be elected every two years and shall hold their respective offices for a term of two years.

claim: Township electors may merge the clerk and treasurer into one office
quote: The same person may hold the offices of township clerk and treasurer if a majority of the electors present vote in favor of the merging of such offices

claim: If no township meeting is noticed, the county commission appoints the township officers
quote: the board of county commissioners of the county in which the township is located shall appoint the necessary township officers

claim: A school board has five, seven or nine members
quote: The board of a school district must be composed of five, seven, or nine members.

claim: School board members serve three-year terms
quote: The term of each elected member of a school board is three years

claim: Each school board holds an annual election between 1 April and 30 June
quote: The board of a school district shall hold an election each year between April first and June thirtieth

claim: A school board may hold its election with a city's regular election
quote: the annual election may be held in conjunction with the regular election of a city

claim: The school election ballot must be nonpartisan in form
quote: The ballot must be nonpartisan in form

claim: School candidates file a document with their name and position sought
quote: shall prepare and sign a document stating the individual's name and the position for which that individual is a candidate

claim: The school candidate with the most votes is elected
quote: The individual receiving the highest number of votes for an office must be declared elected.

claim: Soil conservation district supervisors are elected at the general election
quote: The regular election of soil conservation districts must be held at the same time, and at the same place, as the general election is held.

claim: Soil conservation candidates go on the no-party ballot
quote: the name of the candidate so nominated on the no-party ballot at the ensuing general election

claim: Soil conservation district supervisors serve six-year terms
quote: one district supervisor must be elected for a term of six years

claim: Southwest Water Authority directors are elected, one per member county plus two in Dickinson and one in Mandan
quote: One director must be elected from each county within the authority, two directors must be elected in the city of Dickinson, and one director must be elected in the city of Mandan.

claim: Southwest Water Authority candidates appear on the no-party primary ballot and the highest vote wins
quote: aspirant on the no-party primary election ballot as a candidate for the office of director. The candidate receiving the highest number of votes is elected.

claim: The Southwest Water Authority covers Dunn, Stark, Golden Valley, Billings, Slope, Bowman, Adams, Grant, Hettinger, Morton and Mercer counties, and adjoining counties may join
quote: the boundaries of Dunn, Stark, Golden Valley, Billings, Slope, Bowman, Adams, Grant, Hettinger, Morton, and Mercer Counties

claim: An adjoining county may join the Southwest Water Authority with the board's approval
quote: Any county adjoining the authority as herein created, or as hereafter composed, may join such authority

claim: The party sections of the primary ballot carry congressional, legislative and state offices
quote: The primary election ballot for party nominations shall contain the following offices in the following order under each party column:

claim: A certificate of nomination may be a certificate by petition for independent nominations
quote: The certificate of nomination by petition for independent nominations provided for by this chapter

claim: County candidates file a petition with the county auditor
quote: Every candidate for a county office shall present a petition to the county auditor

claim: Southwest Water Authority directors for Dickinson and Mandan file with the city auditor
quote: aspires to the office of director of the southwest water authority shall, before four p.m. on the

claim: The executive officer is the mayor in council cities and the president of the board of city commissioners in commission cities
quote: "Executive officer" means the mayor in council cities or the president of the board of city commissioners in commission cities.
